Arcsin(+Infinity) is a directed infinity along the negative imaginary axis: $\arcsin(x) \to \pi/2 - i\infty$ as $x \to +\infty$
Arcsin(-Infinity) is the opposite directed infinity, by oddness: $\arcsin(-x) = -\arcsin(x)$
Not simply 2: $2$ is outside the principal range $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$, so $\arcsin(\sin 2) = \pi - 2$
Arcsin(ComplexInfinity) is Indeterminate -- the real +Infinity and -Infinity directions alone already disagree ($-i\infty$ vs $+i\infty$)
